newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares trim losses, eyes on telecom merger.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares trim losses, eyes on telecom merger.

text.p: Italian shares trimmed losses to end just slightly lower on Monday after interest was sparked in telecom shares when Italy's Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi announced a plan to merger STET with Telecom Italia.

Telecom holding group STET shares rose sharply as its attractions were suddenly unveiled as it would lose its "holding company" tag which has acted as a weight on its shares price, while Telecom Italia shares slide in response as its attraction as a "peer player" in the telecom sector took a knock.
The all-share Mibtel index ended off 0.25 percent at 9,951 while the Mib30 index finished down 0.43 percent at 14,913.

The Italian Treasury said it had instructed state holding group IRI to merge STET with Telecom Italia. IRI currently holds 64 percent of STET, while STET holds a majority of shares in Telecom Italia. The Treasury also postponed the flotation of STET to the autumn of 1997 from the start of 1997.

Analysts said the merger appeared to be a move to maximise the proceeds from the STET privatisation, and many had seen STET shares trading at a price discount to other telecom stocks because of its holding company structure.
STET shares ended up 6.18 percent at 5,674 lire while Telecom Italia slide some 7.85 percent to 3,321 lire.

Among other shares, Olivetti ended up 5.77 percent at 478.7 lire after the group announced late on Friday that it was selling an indirect stake of 5.8 percent in mobile phone consortium Omnitel for 432.5 billion lire to Mannesmann.
Most other shares were generally easier with ENI off 0.46 percent at 7,381 lire, Pirelli down 0.81 percent at 2,682 lire and Montedison 1.65 percent easier at 1,056 lire.

News that the centre-right opposition and the Northern League are to boycott the vote over the 1997 budget procedure helped ease some fears over the passage of the measure through the lower house of parliament.
